title: Node provisioning odyssey — weekly notes and install journal
content:
Purpose:
Weekly working journal for ongoing node provisioning and install work across VPC + on-prem customers. This doc is the canonical standup notes for the week of 2026-03-02 — capture of handoffs, persistent blockers, and next-step experiments. Not an RFC; rough, action-oriented.

Attendees / async contributors:
- Aisha Banerjee (owner)
- Liam Chen (install eng)
- Maya Ortiz (network field eng)
- Noah Patel (site reliability)
- Sofie Müller (customer success on Acme Analytics)

High-level summary:
- Made progress on three customer installs: Acme Analytics (on-prem GPU cluster), Helix Labs (VPC peering + BGP), and Fortuna Health (edge appliance rollouts).
- Common recurring theme: network path MTU and firewall rules causing opaque failures during big-container image pulls and NVLink interconnect tests.
- Telemetry shows intermittent model-runner OOMs on 80GB A100 nodes when KV cache warmup collides with large-batch warmup — likely a memory-accounting gap in the model-runner 1.9.2 container.

Customer-specific notes:
1) Acme Analytics (on-prem):
- Status: install in final validation phase.
- Blocker: NFS mount flapping when /opt/redwood/runtime is heavy (inode exhaustion observed on event timestamps 03/03 02:14 and 03/04 11:33). We suspect mount options + aggressive GC from their backup agent.
- Action taken: Disabled backup agent on 3 nodes, remounted with noatime,nodiratime; increased inodes on test replica.
- Next: run 48h soak, and if stable, add fstype-specific mount flags to installer templating. Owner: Liam.

2) Helix Labs (VPC peering):
- Status: partial; control-plane routes established but data-plane blackhole persists for 10G egress flows.
- Root cause hypothesis: MTU mismatch on the transit device + AWS ENI offload mismatch; large TCP segments are being dropped, which surface as TLS handshake timeouts for large model pulls.
- Workaround: force TCP MSS clamp to 1400 on the peering route; verified immediate improvement for image pulls > 600MB.
- Permanent fix: coordinate with Helix networking to align MTU and offload settings; add an automated MSS-clamp step to the VPC peer playbook. Owner: Maya.

3) Fortuna Health (edge appliance):
- Status: rollouts paused on 4 of 12 appliances due to driver mismatches.
- Observed: NVIDIA driver 535.x vs container CUDA tooling expecting 525.x — model-runner crashes during nvml init.
- Action: rolled back to validated driver build on 4 appliances; preparing a trimmed container image that tolerates both driver families. Owner: Noah.

Shared technical findings / telemetry:
- Model-runner 1.9.2 shows a pattern: memory footprint spikes right after KV cache initialization when model is first warmed with 64-token prompts and batch sizes > 8. Repro steps included in linked PR. Temporary mitigation is to serialize the warmup (warm by model shards rather than whole cluster).
- Installer logs show increased EC2 API throttling when parallelizing AMI builds across 40 nodes. Throttle produces partial AMI failures that the installer currently treats as fatal. We should add exponential backoff + retry with idempotent tags.
- Observability gap: node-level GPU telemetry is not being captured across the NATed subnets for some installs. Root cause appears to be an iptables rule inherited from onprem baseline that drops UDP for our telemetry agent.

Standup rollup (daily items we tracked this week):
- Mon 03/02: ran soak tests on Acme test rack; discovered inode pressure.
- Tue 03/03: validated MSS clamp on Helix test VPC; image pull success rate up 78%.
- Wed 03/04: rolled back drivers on Fortuna pilot group; started trimmed image build.
- Thu 03/05: investigated model-runner OOM trace and opened PR with instrumented heap markers.
- Fri 03/06: consolidated field notes and prepared customer-facing handoff decks.

Open blockers (priority ordered):
- B1: Inode exhaustion + flaky NFS (Acme) — high customer impact; ETA for mitigation: 48h after soak. Owner: Liam.
- B2: MTU/ENI offload mismatch causing large-image failures (Helix) — high; requires network team coordination. Owner: Maya.
- B3: Model-runner memory-accounting regression on 1.9.2 — medium; engineering to prototype serialized warmup. Owner: Aisha + Research.
- B4: Telemetry UDP being dropped on NATed subnets — medium; add netfilter audit and adjust iptables template. Owner: Noah.

Action items (who / what / due):
- Liam: implement inode increase and add installer guard for inode checks (due 2026-03-09).
- Maya: draft VPC peer MSS-clamp step and schedule joint troubleshooting with Helix network (due 2026-03-08).
- Noah: finish trimmed runtime image that tolerates 525–535 drivers; produce test matrix (due 2026-03-10).
- Aisha: push model-runner serialized-warmup prototype into staging and measure QPS/latency impact (due 2026-03-11).
- Sofie: prepare customer update emails for Acme and Helix summarizing workaround and ETA (due 2026-03-07).

Decisions and notes for product/installer changes:
- Add an installer preflight that checks inode counts and fails fast with clear remediation steps.
- Add optional MSS clamp toggle for VPC peering runs (default: off; enable when peering with unknown transit).
- Add exponential backoff to AMI parallelization and surface retryable error codes to operator console.

Follow-ups for next week:
- Run 72h soak on Acme after inode changes and push results into confluence page.
- Validate serialized-warmup on two staging clusters with representative KV load.
- Work with Helix to align ENI offload settings; if not possible, add MSS clamp to their installation profile.
- Add a quick iptables audit check to the installer to detect UDP telemetry blocking rules.

Notes / random observations: 
- Field tip: some customer baseline images have systemd-tmpfiles cleaning policies that aggressively remove /var/lib/locker and can blow away container caches — add a check for tmpfiles.d entries in the preflight.
- Logging suggestion: include node-level kubelet arguments and AMI build tag in every install artifact to help correlate postmortems.

Appendix (short reproductions and command snippets):
- Quick MSS clamp verification on Linux host: 
  sudo iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --set-mss 1400

- Check inode counts: 
  df -ih /opt/redwood/runtime

- Minimal reproduce for model-runner warmup OOM:
  1) start cluster with model-runner 1.9.2
  2) run 4 concurrent warmup scripts: ./warmup.sh --batch 12 --tokens 64 x4
  3) monitor /proc/*/smaps and dmesg for OOM killer entries

If you want something split into a formal RFC or an ops playbook, say so and I will extract the install-relevant sections. Otherwise this doc will be the running worklog until next Friday.
